hero.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins' wife of operating anonymous social media accounts attacking Governor
hero.body:
Multiple social media accounts were shut down after prominent members of Governor Ron DeSantis' communications team claimed that Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins, had been operating them to attack the Governor and promote her husband's campaign for the Republican gubernatorial nomination. Christina Pushaw, a Communications Specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, both publicly presented evidence linking the accounts to the Second Lady.

Robert Salvador, CEO of Promota, conducted research showing that the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number and email address similar to ones associated with Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots through two-factor authentication documentation, which displayed an access attempt that triggered messages to a partially concealed email address and phone number showing only the final digits. Pushaw identified a second account, @bobnamy1, which she also claimed was tied to Layla Collins. According to Pushaw, the content of these accounts focused exclusively on two activities: supporting Jay Collins and attacking individuals who refused to endorse him, including Governor DeSantis.

Redfern corroborated these allegations, confirming that the FSUDude account connected directly to Layla Collins' personal cell phone number. Both accounts were deactivated shortly after Pushaw and Redfern made their accusations public. Pushaw questioned the appropriateness of a state board member, appointed by the same Governor being criticized in the posts, maintaining such accounts. Layla Collins serves on the state Board of Education, having been appointed by DeSantis. Florida Politics requested comment from both Jay and Layla Collins.

Both Pushaw and Redfern have prior experience in DeSantis' communications operation, having previously served as Press Secretary to the Governor. Redfern currently works for Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Representative Byron Donalds for Governor. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year. Collins is now competing for the Republican gubernatorial nomination alongside Donalds, former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner, and investment manager James Fishback. The timing of these accusations coincides with Collins' active campaign efforts within the Republican primary race.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds extends fundraising dominance in Florida Governor's race with $90 million raised
cards.teaser: U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds has raised $90 million for his gubernatorial campaign, with nearly $10 million in his campaign account and more than $76.2 million to his political committee.
cards.body:
U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds has raised $90 million in his bid for the Republican gubernatorial nomination, according to his campaign. Division of Elections records through June 26 show nearly $10 million in contributions to his campaign account and more than $76.2 million to the Friends of Byron Donalds political committee. Between June 20 and June 26, Donalds raised nearly $2 million, with major contributors including GOPAC Election Fund, Ferreira Construction of New Jersey, Phillips Infrastructure of Tennessee, and the Southern Group. Donalds recently launched a $20 million statewide ad buy on television and digital platforms. He has secured endorsements from U.S. Sen. Ashley Moody, Attorney General James Uthmeier, Agriculture Secretary Wilton Simpson, CFO Blaise Ingoglia, incoming Florida Senate President Jim Boyd, and Florida House Speaker-designate Sam Garrison.

His opponents trail significantly in fundraising. Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins raised nearly $15,500 in hard money and just $100 to his Quiet Professionals FL political committee during the week ending June 26, with less than $3.5 million total as of that date. Former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner and investment manager James Fishback continue to fall further behind. The Republican primary is scheduled for August 18.

cards.headline: 40-year-old driver killed in head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County
cards.body:
A fatal head-on collision claimed the life of a 40-year-old driver on State Road 710 in Martin County early Sunday morning. The crash occurred around 2 a.m. near the intersection of State Road 710, also known as Beeline Highway, and Southwest Silver Fox Lane, according to the Florida Highway Patrol.

The incident involved a 2015 Kia Optima traveling north on State Road 710 when its driver crossed into the southbound lane and struck a 2021 Toyota Tundra head-on. The front left sections of both vehicles collided with significant force. The impact caused the Kia to catch fire, and it eventually stopped on the grass shoulder facing north. The Tundra came to rest in the southbound lane facing southeast. The 40-year-old driver of the Kia died at the scene. The Tundra's driver, a 41-year-old from Indiantown, was transported to the hospital by LifeStar medical helicopter.

The crash adds to a troubling pattern on the roadway. Martin County Fire Rescue has responded to 42 vehicle accident-related calls on State Road 710 in just the current year. This latest fatality follows another deadly crash in January that prompted Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek to describe the road as a "death trap." The repeated incidents have raised serious concerns about the safety of the two-lane highway.

Road improvements are underway, though long-term solutions remain years away. The Florida Department of Transportation has scheduled a major expansion project to widen State Road 710 from two lanes to four, but construction is not expected to begin until 2031. While that project moves forward in planning stages, FDOT has initiated interim improvements to the roadway. These current enhancements include pavement work, updated markings and signage, and new turn lanes intended to improve safety conditions in the near term.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Nine-Game Skid With Late Comeback Win Over Tarpons
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trail
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trailed 5-1 after six innings before scoring two runs in the seventh and seven more in the eighth to avoid a six-game sweep. Tampa had been trying to become the first team to sweep a six-game series against the Mets at Clover Park since Minor League Baseball adopted the format in 2021.

The decisive rally came in the eighth inning, when the Mets sent 13 batters to the plate and scored seven runs on four hits, three walks and two hit batters.

Catcher Francisco Toledo delivered the go-ahead hit with one out, ripping a two-run ground-rule double off Jordalin Mendoza to give St. Lucie a 6-5 lead. Taylor Darden followed with a two-run single against Parker Seay to extend the advantage to 8-5. Antonio Jimenez added an RBI infield single, and AJ Salgado drew a bases-loaded walk to cap the inning.

Tampa appeared in control earlier in the game. Engelth Urena homered in the fifth inning to stretch the Tarpons' lead to 5-1.

The Mets' first two runs came on solo home runs. Jimenez tied the game 1-1 in the first inning with his third homer of the season. Branny De Oleo added his sixth home run of the year in the seventh, cutting the deficit to 5-2.

St. Lucie kept the seventh-inning push going when Jeremy Rodriguez doubled and Jack Scanlon followed with an RBI double off Mendoza, bringing the Mets within 5-3.

Mets starter Emilio Obispo made his second appearance of the series and allowed one unearned run over three innings.

The bullpen kept St. Lucie within range after Calvin Ziegler allowed three runs in one-third of an inning during a MiLB rehab appearance. Justin Scarborough allowed only Urena's solo homer over 1.1 innings. Caden Wooster followed with 2.1 scoreless innings, and Ernesto Mercedes worked the final 1.2 innings without allowing a run to earn the win.

Jimenez led the Mets offensively, going 3-for-4 with a home run, three RBI and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 2-for-3 with a double and two runs, while Trey Snyder finished 2-for-4.

The Mets improved to 3-10 in the second half and 36-43 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game commuter series Tuesday against the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: U.S. soccer team faces Belgium in World Cup knockout round Monday with key player suspended
cards.teaser: The United States men's national team takes the field Monday night against Belgium in the Round of 16 at Lumen Field in Seattle, playing without suspended forward Folarin Balogun.
cards.body:
The U.S. men's national team faces Belgium on Monday night in the Round of 16 at Lumen Field in Seattle. The Americans earned the program's first knockout stage victory since 2002 by defeating Bosnia and Herzegovina 2-0 on Wednesday night, though they played the final 26 minutes plus stoppage time with 10 men after Folarin Balogun was red-carded. Longtime referee Andy Davies told ESPN the call was wrong, saying the contact was purely accidental and an unfortunate result from two players challenging for possession in a normal football movement. Coach Mauricio Pochettino said flatly it was never a red card. The American camp noted that Lionel Messi made a nearly identical challenge against Algeria earlier in the tournament and received nothing. Weston McKennie said he thinks it's bogus.

Balogun, one of the team's top players, will watch Monday from the stands against Belgium, which earned a Round of 16 win over the United States in the 2014 World Cup. Belgium has won six consecutive meetings against the U.S. since the inaugural 1930 World Cup, including a 5-2 friendly rout in March. However, the U.S. won Wednesday without Balogun for the final half-hour and will play at a venue where the home crowd will provide strong support.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% to $73.82 for meal for 10, with ground beef and strawberries seeing biggest increases
cards.teaser: A Fourth of July cookout for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
cards.body:
A Fourth of July cookout for 10 people now costs $73.82, up 4% from last year, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey. Inflation is driving the price increases across multiple staple foods. Ground beef is up 5.5%, hamburger buns are up 7.7%, and strawberries, damaged by a Florida frost, have surged 12.4% in price. Ice cream prices have also climbed 5.3% year over year.

Not all cookout items have become more expensive. Potato prices have declined this year, offering savings for those planning to serve potato chips or potato salad. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades region can offer better deals. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends shopping strategically to manage costs. "It's really important to shop savvier than ever, it is comparing the stores to see who has the best deals for the groceries on your list, the biggest thing for families is cutting down the food waste, and that begins with a meal plan," Woroch said.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation in Fort Pierce offers artist residency program and public tours of historic Crain Estate
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation in Fort Pierce is transforming the city into an artistic destination through its artist-in-residency program and public tours of the historic Crain Estate.
cards.body:
The non-profit organization preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, who once called the property home. Mr. Crain was a tile worker by trade, and his craftsmanship is visible throughout the entire facility from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, with 90% of the estate remaining the way it was when the Crains lived there.

The Peacock House gets its name from the birds that have roamed the property for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, bringing in seven originally that have multiplied to over 100. Among the flock is a beloved bird named Bob, believed to be 60 years old, who walks with a limp and is hand fed every day.

The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world, offering simple but elegant accommodations on the property. The art lab offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels. Krystal Masters, the art director, leads one-on-one classes designed to be accessible to complete beginners, with students coming in with zero experience and walking out with a piece of art.

hero.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation attracts international artists to Fort Pierce with residency program
hero.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination with an artist-in-residency program that attracts artists from around the world and offers classes for children and adults.
hero.body:
Rewritten Card Body

Tucked away in the historic Crain Estate, the Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination by preserving the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain. Art director Krystal Masters notes that Mr. Crain was a tile worker by trade, and his craftsmanship is visible throughout the entire facility, from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. The couple traveled the world 9 times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their Florida estate, including a gazebo shipped from India that features tiny peacocks. The estate remains approximately 90 percent unchanged from when the Crains lived there, including distinctive spaces like the smoking and bourbon room with its man paneling and stained glass. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world and offers simple but elegant accommodations on the property. No professional experience is required to participate. The art lab provides classes for children and adults of all skill levels, with Masters leading one-on-one classes accessible to complete beginners in sculpting and watercolor. The Peacock House gets its name from the birds that have roamed the property for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced seven peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, and the population has grown to over 100. Among the flock is Bob, believed to be 60 years old and recognized by his distinctive limp.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie City Council to vote on giving 7 acres to FDOT for Florida Turnpike interchange at Midway Road
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange at Florida's Turnpike. Final approval is expected at an upcoming meeting.
cards.body:
Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange at Florida's Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie. The interchange is designed to accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth that will occur over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. According to the FDOT website for the project, the second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase and construction is anticipated to begin in Summer 2027.

The partial interchange is still in the design phase. Erin Scheumeister, a Port St. Lucie resident, said the construction can be annoying but she believes it is necessary. The Midway Road Widening Project will also add bike and pedestrian paths, along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Marine Unit rescues two boaters after vessel sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday, thanks to a quick response from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit and the life-saving decision to wear life jackets.
cards.body:
Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged on July 1. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded. Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but deputies say they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived.

Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. The sheriff's office said in a Facebook post that the incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life. "We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call," the agency stated.

cards.teaser: A Fourth of July meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey. Ground beef is up 5.5%, buns are up 7.7% and strawberries are up 12.4%.
cards.body:
According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. The survey points to inflation as the primary driver of price increases. Ground beef is up 5.5%, and buns are up 7.7%. Strawberries, hit hard by a Florida frost, are up 12.4%. Ice cream is up 5.3%.

Not everything is more expensive this year. Potato prices are down, which is good news for potato chip and salad lovers. Corn prices have fluctuated, but locally grown corn from the Glades can offer the best deal. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch said shoppers should compare stores to find the best deals for groceries on their list. She also emphasized that cutting down on food waste is crucial for families, and that process begins with a meal plan.

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closes today for $3 million renovation to nearly double slip capacity
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a year-long renovation project funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees. The $3 million project is expected to be complete by next Fourth of July. When finished, the dock will nearly double its capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock, and a smaller floating platform. Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades serve a purpose beyond adding capacity. "They're doing it to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms," Reed said. "So the year of waiting will be worth it."

During the closure, the city is working to accommodate businesses that depend on the dock. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates passenger tours from the dock, initially had concerns about continuing operations during construction. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the city found a solution by allowing the company to build a gate at the end of the non-floating section for boarding passengers. Kuyrkendall acknowledged the dock's current limitations on busy weekends and supported the modernization. "Stuart is not Stuart without the water," Kuyrkendall said. Boat captain Parker Fisher, based in Stuart, also expressed support for the project. "It's definitely needed some work over the years, so I'm glad they're putting money into it," Fisher said.

hero.headline: Serena Williams withdraws from Wimbledon doubles with sister Venus due to knee injury
hero.teaser: Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday because of a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week.
hero.body:
Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week. The 44-year-old lost her singles match 6-3, 6-7 (6), 6-3 to 20-year-old Maya Joint of Australia on Tuesday. In an Instagram post, Serena said she did everything she could but her knee wasn't ready to compete. She posted images of four syringes showing fluid drained from her knee after her singles match, along with a video showing her walking with strapping on her right leg and what appeared to be one of her daughters holding a cane for her.

The Williams sisters were scheduled to play Camila Osorio and Solana Sierra in the only first-round doubles match that wasn't scheduled earlier in the week. The match had been pushed back to give Serena more time to recover. Venus, 46, competed in mixed doubles on Friday with Kevin Krawietz, losing in straight sets to Tereza Mihalikova and Lloyd Glasspool. With the U.S. Open approaching, Serena indicated she could play again soon, telling fans to "stay tuned to a city near you." The Williams sisters are six-time champions as partners in women's doubles at Wimbledon.

cards.headline: Defending World Cup champion Argentina survives 3-2 scare from Cape Verde in extra time
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi and Argentina beat Cape Verde 3-2 on Friday in a thrilling World Cup Round of 32 match that went to extra time before the reigning champions advanced to face Egypt.
cards.body:
Argentina advanced to the World Cup Round of 16 after defeating Cape Verde 3-2 in a match that required extra time to decide. The go-ahead score came in the 111th minute when Cristian Romero's header deflected off Cape Verde's Diney Borges for an own goal. Messi scored in the 29th minute for his record-extending 20th career World Cup goal, and Lisandro Martinez scored in the 103rd minute to put Argentina ahead 2-1.

Sidny Lopes Cabral and Deroy Duarte scored equalizers for Cape Verde that stunned the pro-Argentina crowd in South Florida. Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, 40 years old, made 10 saves against Argentina, including five against Messi. Cape Verde became the smallest country to reach the knockout round after securing draws against Spain, Uruguay, and Saudi Arabia in group play.

Argentina will face Egypt in Atlanta on Tuesday. Messi has seven goals in this tournament, one more than France's Kylian Mbappé in the Golden Boot race, and has 12 goals during his record eight-match scoring streak.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football team finished last season with a 10-2 record and a district title, but a second-round playoff exit has motivated them to pursue a state championship during the 2026 fall season. Head coach Jimmy Robertson is counting on a veteran senior class to lead the program forward. Most of the seniors have been with the program for four years, with many coming through the middle school ranks. Robertson said this continuity positions the team for success, stating that "hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had."

To elevate their competition level, the Scots have scheduled more challenging opponents for 2026. Senior Jack Williams explained that the team wants to compete at the next level by facing quality opponents and attracting new people to the program. Senior Jack Whelche emphasized that playoff success is the true measure of improvement, noting that going undefeated in the regular season means nothing if the team continues losing in the second round of the playoffs. As the Scots prepare through summer workouts, senior Edmyer St. Jean said the daily training "adds up every day as something like to look forward to" and gives the team reason to push harder for positive results when the season begins.

U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds has raised $90 million in his bid for the Republican gubernatorial nomination, according to his campaign. Division of Elections records through June 26 show nearly $10 million in contributions to his campaign account and more than $76.2 million to the Friends of Byron Donalds political committee. Between June 20 and June 26, Donalds raised nearly $2 million, with major contributors including GOPAC Election Fund, Ferreira Construction of New Jersey, Phillips Infrastructure of Tennessee, and the Southern Group. Donalds recently launched a $20 million statewide ad buy on television and digital platforms. He has secured endorsements from U.S. Sen. Ashley Moody, Attorney General James Uthmeier, Agriculture Secretary Wilton Simpson, CFO Blaise Ingoglia, incoming Florida Senate President Jim Boyd, and Florida House Speaker-designate Sam Garrison.

His opponents trail significantly in fundraising. Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins raised nearly $15,500 in hard money and just $100 to his Quiet Professionals FL political committee during the week ending June 26, with less than $3.5 million total as of that date. Former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner and investment manager James Fishback continue to fall further behind. The Republican primary is scheduled for August 18.

cards.headline: U.S. soccer team faces Belgium in World Cup knockout round Monday with key player suspended
cards.teaser: The United States men's national team takes the field Monday night against Belgium in the Round of 16 at Lumen Field in Seattle, playing without suspended forward Folarin Balogun.
cards.body:
The U.S. men's national team faces Belgium on Monday night in the Round of 16 at Lumen Field in Seattle. The Americans earned the program's first knockout stage victory since 2002 by defeating Bosnia and Herzegovina 2-0 on Wednesday night, though they played the final 26 minutes plus stoppage time with 10 men after Folarin Balogun was red-carded. Longtime referee Andy Davies told ESPN the call was wrong, saying the contact was purely accidental and an unfortunate result from two players challenging for possession in a normal football movement. Coach Mauricio Pochettino said flatly it was never a red card. The American camp noted that Lionel Messi made a nearly identical challenge against Algeria earlier in the tournament and received nothing. Weston McKennie said he thinks it's bogus.

Balogun, one of the team's top players, will watch Monday from the stands against Belgium, which earned a Round of 16 win over the United States in the 2014 World Cup. Belgium has won six consecutive meetings against the U.S. since the inaugural 1930 World Cup, including a 5-2 friendly rout in March. However, the U.S. won Wednesday without Balogun for the final half-hour and will play at a venue where the home crowd will provide strong support.

cards.headline: President Trump dominates 250th anniversary celebrations as critics draw comparisons to monarchy
cards.teaser: The 250th anniversary of America's independence kicked off with a campaign-style rally by President Donald Trump on the National Mall, as his actions lead to comparisons with King George III.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump held a campaign-style rally on the National Mall as the 250th anniversary of American independence began, with his face appearing on banners fluttering from federal buildings across the nation's capital. Since returning to office in January 2025, Trump has nominated one of his personal lawyers to serve as attorney general, ordered the Department of Justice to pursue his political enemies, deployed the U.S. Marines to the nation's second largest city, and leveraged the presidency to enrich himself and his family. He has demanded that comedians who mock him be fired, slapped his name on the Kennedy Center, pushed to seize control of elections, filed lawsuits against news organizations whose coverage he disliked, and sued his own government seeking $10 billion in taxpayer money. Trump's celebrations have overshadowed the bipartisan, congressionally authorized commission that was supposed to coordinate the anniversary events. He plans to return to the National Mall on July Fourth for what he calls a "Trump rally."

The imagery and Trump's actions have led to comparisons with King George III, the British monarch whose rule inspired the American Revolution. When King Charles III visited Trump this year, the official White House X account posted an image of the two men with the caption "TWO KINGS." At the start of his second term, Trump posted "LONG LIVE THE KING" after declaring he had ended a New York City transportation program. Trump has rejected such comparisons, telling CBS "60 Minutes" earlier this year: "I'm not a king. If I was a king, I wouldn't be dealing with you."

cards.headline: Americans mark 250 years of independence with tempered celebrations amid political discord
cards.teaser: Across the United States, Americans are celebrating the country's 250th birthday by tuning out partisan conflict and focusing on personal concepts of resilience and community.
cards.body:
Across the United States, Americans are celebrating their country's 250th birthday by tuning out partisan discord and focusing on their personal concepts of America. In Associated Press interviews with citizens before the Fourth of July, auto technician Joe Fuqua-Bejarano in Topeka, Kansas, said resilience rather than politics makes Americans awesome. "We've just all got to find unity somewhere, whether that's in laughter or perseverance, and keep everybody cool," he said from his fireworks stand.

Christina Zhou, a 25-year-old research assistant from Cambridge, Massachusetts, acknowledged there are many points of contention but noted beautiful things are still happening. She said she focuses on local events because they feel more within personal control. In Mont Vernon, New Hampshire, farmer Mindy Dean, 50, and her family plan to milk their goats and possibly attend local fireworks. "We're just happy Americans," she said. "We kinda do our own thing and just enjoy our freedom as Americans." In contrast, 81-year-old retiree Neil Casey from Nashua, New Hampshire, and his friend Maureen Regan from Cambridge are visiting Boston's historical sites including Paul Revere's house and attending Fourth of July events. Regan took heart in World Cup soccer fans who visited the country, saying they appreciate what Americans have and urging compatriots to remember how fortunate they are.

cards.headline: European welfare states face demographic pressure as World Cup visitors showcase generous vacation policies
cards.teaser: European visitors to the United States for the World Cup benefit from at least four weeks of paid annual leave under European Union rules, but aging populations threaten the sustainability of social programs.
cards.body:
European workers enjoy more generous vacation policies than Americans, with EU rules guaranteeing at least four weeks of paid annual leave, though many countries provide additional time through collective agreements. However, this benefit comes with a significant tax burden. According to the OECD's 2025 tax-wedge numbers, Belgium leads at 52.5% for a single average worker, followed by Germany at 49.3%, France at 47.2%, Austria at 47.1%, and Italy at 45.8%, compared to the OECD average of 35.1%. The tax wedge measures the gap between what it costs to employ a worker and what that worker takes home after income tax and social-security contributions.

Europe's generous welfare state was built for populations with more children, stronger growth, and more young contributors. This model now faces demographic pressure as 22% of the EU population was already 65 or older on January 1, 2025. Eurostat projects the working-age share of the EU population, those aged 20 to 64, will fall from 58% in 2025 to 50% by 2100. Germany exemplifies this strain, with its public pension system depending heavily on current workers funding current retirees. The regular retirement age is already rising to 67 for Germans born in 1964 or later. A government-appointed pension commission has discussed a Swedish-style funded pension element, mandatory contributions, and a gradual increase in retirement age linked to life expectancy, which Reuters reported could eventually push retirement toward 70.

hero.headline: 40-year-old driver killed in head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County
hero.body:
A 40-year-old man died early Sunday morning following a head-on collision on State Road 710 in Martin County, the Florida Highway Patrol reported. The crash occurred around 2 a.m. near the intersection of State Road 710, also known as Beeline Highway, and Southwest Silver Fox Lane. A northbound 2015 Kia Optima crossed into the southbound lane and struck a 2021 Toyota Tundra in a direct collision. The impact caused the Kia to burst into flames, and it came to rest on the grass shoulder facing north. The Tundra remained in the southbound lane, facing southeast. The Kia driver was pronounced dead at the scene. The Tundra driver, a 41-year-old man from Indiantown, was airlifted to the hospital by LifeStar medical helicopter.

The deadly crash is just the latest in a troubling pattern on the roadway. Martin County Fire Rescue has responded to 42 vehicle accident calls on State Road 710 this year alone. Following a fatal crash in January, Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek described the road as a "death trap." Residents and local officials have grown increasingly frustrated with safety conditions on the stretch of highway. Bill Townsend, who lives near the road, pointed to driver behavior as a contributing factor. "People don't pay a whole lot of attention to other people on the road, and it's kind of a dangerous road sometimes," Townsend said. "Everybody's always in a hurry... just living here makes me worry about the young people learning to drive and learning to drive on that road concerns me, because I have young kids."

State officials have long-term plans to address the road's safety issues. The Florida Department of Transportation intends to widen State Road 710 from two lanes to four lanes, though construction is not expected to begin until 2031. This timeline has drawn criticism from local leaders who question how many more fatalities will occur before improvements are completed. "The question will be how many more people have to die before we get that project going. Florida touts that they have the safest roads in the country but this road is one that clearly is not in that category," Budensiek said in January.

While residents await major construction, FDOT has launched interim improvements including pavement repairs, updated markings, new signage, and additional turn lanes. However, Townsend and other residents say these measures are insufficient. "It would be beneficial to the people that live and travel that road all the time if something happened faster," Townsend said, emphasizing the urgent need for more comprehensive safety improvements to prevent further tragedies.

hero.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation preserves Crain Estate history and brings international artists to Fort Pierce
hero.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation is establishing Fort Pierce as an artistic destination by preserving the historic Crain Estate and operating an artist-in-residency program that welcomes creators from around the world. The nonprofit organization maintains the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, who previously lived on the property in the Peacock Arts District. Jaxson Crain worked as a tile worker, and his skilled craftsmanship remains visible throughout the facility on floors, walls, and ceilings. The estate has retained approximately 90 percent of its original character from the Crains' occupancy, including a smoking and bourbon room featuring wood paneling, traditional masculine colors, and stained glass that opens onto a front patio bar. Visitors can experience the lush gardens and distinctive architecture through guided tours offered every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

The Crains developed their estate through extensive world travel, having journeyed internationally nine times and collected unique items for their Florida home. Among their acquisitions was a gazebo shipped from India, decorated with small peacocks. The couple is credited with introducing peacocks to Fort Pierce during the 1970s, initially bringing seven birds that have since multiplied to over 100. The estate's most famous peacock resident is Bob, believed to be 60 years old, who is recognizable by his limp. Bob receives special treatment, living in his own designated space with individual bowls and receiving hand-feeding from staff members daily. The foundation has deliberately prioritized preserving the estate's authentic character while avoiding excessive commercialization.

The foundation's artist-in-residency program draws international artists by offering simple yet elegant accommodations on the property. These spaces provide everything artists need while maintaining understated elegance. The art lab provides classes for both children and adults regardless of skill level or prior experience. Krystal Masters, the art director, teaches one-on-one classes specifically designed for beginners who arrive with no artistic background. "The majority of my classes are one on one classes you come in with zero experience and you walk out with a piece of art and it makes you feel good," Masters said. Classes cover various mediums including sculpting and watercolor, with current workshops such as "paint your pet in watercolor and rainbow" available to participants.

Beyond its focus on preservation and professional art, the foundation emphasizes art's therapeutic value. Masters views art as stress relief, noting that participants "leave happy and haven't been on their phone scrolling." The foundation's commitment extends to memorable experiences for all visitors, particularly children who interact with the peacocks during tours. The organization has also preserved stories of the Crains' eccentric lifestyle, including the anecdote that Jaxson Crain once returned from South America with a baby monkey he had carried in his pocket. Through these interconnected programs, the Peacock House Art Foundation continues to honor the Crains' adventurous spirit while connecting local and international artists within the broader Peacock Arts District community.
